name: Aptitude Test 01
subtitle: UVTN 2022 · Round 1: CV & Aptitude Test
description: Full-length simulation: 9 verbal reasoning, 10 quantitative reasoning (case exhibits) and 6 abstract reasoning questions in one 30-minute sitting, with no breaks between sections.
keyNote: The answer key follows the bolded options in the original test file; that file has no written explanations.

questions.intro: One of the most prestigious awards that a fiction author can win is the Man Booker Prize for Fiction. Since its advent in 1969, it has been awarded every year for the best original full-length novel written in the English language by a citizen of the Commonwealth of Nations, Ireland or Zimbabwe. The prize money awarded with the Booker Prize was originally £21,000. It stayed the same until it was raised to £50,000 in 2002 after it was sponsored by the Man Group. It has remained at this level since then. This has made it one of the world’s richest literary prizes. From the time the prize was launched in 1969 until 2012, 23 of the winners have been from the UK. Hilary Mantel won in 2009 and 2012 with two sequential novels of the same genre. The winner in 2012 was the historical fiction book, Bring up the Bodies. Other authors who have won the Booker Prize more than once include Peter Carey, who triumphed in 1988 and 2001, and J. M. Coetzee, who took home the prize in 1983 and 1999. In 1993, to mark the 25th anniversary of the Booker Prize, it was decided to choose a ‘Booker of Bookers’ Prize. Three previous judges of the award, Malcolm Bradbury, David Holloway and W. L. Webb chose Midnight’s Children (the 1981 winner) as ‘the best novel out of all the winners’. A similar prize, known as ‘The Best of the Booker’, was awarded in 2008 to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Booker Prize. The winner, after a public vote, was once again Salman Rushdie’s Midnight’s Children.
questions.stem: Statement: The Man Group contributed an extra £29,000 to the prize money for the Booker Prize.
Statement: Hilary Mantel has won £100,000 in prize money from the Booker Prize.

Since the break-up of the monopoly that company A held over the computer industry, the average price of personal computers has declined by 15 percent. Therefore, if the monopoly company V maintaining over the airline industry is broken up, the price for flight tickets will also decrease by 15 percent.
The argument above is based on
options: a potentially naive trust in statistical analysis
an attempt to refute a generalization by means of an exceptional case
a confusion of cause and effect
an analogy between past and future events
an appeal to popular beliefs and values

questions.stem:
Lawyer: Although there is no eyewitness to the crime, it is evident that it must have been committed by Jones, Alyers, or Singh, all of whom were working in the electronics supply warehouse at the time the theft of the case of new tablets occurred. Electronic timestamps indicate that all three men were checking inventory at the time of the theft. Singh, the more senior employee with the higher pay grade, was supervising Jones and Alyers, who were processing the inventory. Singh has already testified that both Jones and Alyers were out of his sight numerous times throughout the shift. Therefore, Jones or Alyers had the most motive and opportunity to commit the theft.
The lawyer’s argument assumes which of the following?
options: All theft by employees of a company is done during the processing of inventory.
Tenure of employment and salary are directly related to the likelihood of committing theft.
Jones was out of Singh’s sight more often than Alyers.
Any testimony in court should be treated skeptically.
The number of trucks with stolen items is growing.

questions.stem:
To tackle the alarming pollution levels in Labyrinth Lake, the state implemented a green campaign to clean the lake water through water refinery, which resulted in a noticeable lower level of pollution. Ironically, the once-abundant population of sunfish in the lake saw a considerable decline during the very same period.
Which of the following, if true, would best explain the apparent paradox?
options: The water refinement process creates an environment extremely favorable to pike, a predator fish.
Several artificial chemicals are introduced into the lake as a result of the refinement process, but these chemicals are known to have a benign effect on fish.
The life spans of sunfish are not diminished by high pollution levels, but the number of offspring they create during their lifetime is diminished.
The heaviest concentrations of sunfish population in the lake are at its northern and northeastern shores, many miles away from the water refinery.
Ever since 2005, a strictly enforced state regulation has prevented anglers from over-fishing Labyrinth Lake.

questions.stem:
Placing cups of hot coffee on a table for customers to pick up inevitably risks a spill that scalds the customer, but directly handing the cups to customers presently carries even more danger of a spill per cup of coffee served. Therefore, we at Coffee Corporation have concluded that the only way to decrease the incidence of coffee spills, while continuing to sell as many cups of coffee as we do now, is to ensure that employees more frequently place cups on a table and less frequently hand them over directly.
Which of the following, if true, most seriously weakens the argument above?
options: Coffee spills caused by handing coffee directly to customers have typically caused more serious scalding than those that occur when customers pick up coffee off a table.
Heat damage that hot coffee can cause a table by resting on it can be limited by careful observation.
Coffee-handling employees can, without difficulty, be trained to hand coffee cups directly to customers with less danger of a coffee spill.
Placing several hot cups of coffee on a table frequently causes unpleasant steam to rise in the vicinity of the table, which handing cups of coffee directly to customers generally avoids.
Handing a coffee cup directly to a customer represents better customer service than placing it on a table does.

questions.stem:
The Mohs scale of mineral hardness categorizes the ability of one natural sample of mineral to make a visible scratch on another mineral. The hardness of a certain mineral A, on the scale, is measured by finding the hardest mineral that mineral A can scratch, or the softest mineral that can scratch mineral A. However, at times, minerals that are classed as lower hardness on the Mohs scale can create microscopic disruptions on minerals that have a higher Mohs hardness. These microscopic disruptions can sometimes damage the structural integrity of the harder mineral.
Which of the following, if true, most helps to explain how minerals lower on the Mohs scale can still affect minerals that are higher on the Mohs scale?
options: Microscopic disruptions are not considered “scratches” for the determination of a Mohs scale number.
The Mohs scale was created in 1812 without the more complete knowledge of mineral hardness that exists today. The softer minerals’ impact on the harder minerals is imperceptible to the naked eye.
Such anomalies do not exist when using the Vickers scale, which is a more precise measure of hardness than the Mohs scale.
Minerals that are scratched often bear some residue of the mineral that inflicted the scratch.
The softer minerals’ impact on the harder minerals is imperceptible to the naked eye.

questions.stem:
Principal: The average grade of honors students on the last test was 98 points. Most students in the school are honors students. Furthermore, the amount of extra credit per test earned by any student generally does not fluctuate from test to test. It is clear that most students in the school earn at least some extra credit.
The principal’s conclusion is most vulnerable to which of the following criticisms?
options: It takes for granted that classes with honors students are typical of the classes at the whole school with regard to the average amount of extra credit earned per test.
It overlooks the possibility that even if, on average, a certain amount of extra credit is earned by some types of students, many students may earn no extra credit at all.

It takes for granted that if a certain average amount of extra credit is earned on a test by each student in the school, then approximately the same amount of extra credit must be earned each test by each honors student.

It confuses a claim from which the argument’s conclusion about the test scores would necessarily follow with a claim that would follow from the argument’s conclusion only with a high degree of probability.
It overlooks the possibility that even if most students in the class earn some extra credit each test, any one student may, on some tests, earn no extra credit.

questions.stem:
The ethics codes of universities should be decided by an external committee rather than by the faculty and students of the universities themselves. The involvement of both students and faculty leaves many decisions subject to changing positions in political thought.
The conclusion drawn above relies most on which of the following assumptions?
options: The faculty and students of most universities are unable to avoid the pressure to accord with changing fashions in political thought.
External committees chosen to judge ethics codes would be relatively less susceptible to the changing fashions in political thought.
Most universities that are trying to form ethics codes are aware of the need to avoid making concessions to the changing fashions of political thought.
External committees chosen to judge ethics codes would be made up of ethics experts.
The involvement of students and faculty in ethics codes has given those codes a decidedly liberal bent.

questions.stem:
In 2021, company A began producing headphone X and sold every unit of X produced. The company’s total cost of manufacturing headphone X was equal to $120,000 plus 6 percent of the company’s total revenue from all units of X sold. If the company made a profit on X in 2021, was the number of units of X being sold greater than 25,000?
(1) The company’s total revenue from the sale of headphone X in 2021 was greater than $130,000.
(2) For each unit of headphone X sold, the company’s revenue was smaller than $6.

In an orientation series, the total number of students joining 4 webinars was 1600. What was the average (arithmetic mean) number of students attending each webinar?
(1) Each student attended at least one webinar.
(2) The average number of webinars attended per student was 2.
Assuming revenues grow at 5% and profits decline at 10% per annum in each segment, the difference between the total cost of category A and category B at the end of FY 2022 will be ___
options: £3bn
We lack sufficient information

questions.stem:

Statements b and c

questions.stem:

b. The region with the lowest total manufacturing costs had the lowest revenues
c. Regions with low overhead costs tend to have higher revenues than regions with high overhead costs
d. Regions with similar manufacturing cost distribution profiles had the same level of revenues
options: Statements a and b
Statements b and c
